clue.text: Technocrat redesigned form of protection

indicators.note: something redesigned has had its parts rearranged into a new layout

blocks.note: the ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A government expert overhauls some form of security policy.
explanation.definitionFit: A long waterproof coat shields its wearer from rain and cold, so it is one kind of protective covering.

clue.text: Archbishop's skirt

blocks.note: first meaning: Desmond ..., the South African archbishop
second meaning: a short stiff frilly skirt worn by ballet dancers

explanation.walkthrough: The 's looks possessive, as if the archbishop owned a skirt, but it stands for 'is' and links the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Desmond Tutu was Archbishop of Cape Town, and a ballerina's stiff layered dress shares the same spelling.

clue.text: PM of Sweden missing the point at first

indicators.note: missing means the named letters are absent from the word

blocks.note: the country, taken as written
south-west is a point of the compass, and here it sits at the start of the word

explanation.surface: A question about the prime minister of a Scandinavian country.
explanation.walkthrough: SW, south-west, is the point taken from the front of SWEDEN, leaving EDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Eden was the British Prime Minister from 1955 to 1957, so he is a former PM.

clue.text: Nobleman taking year to be concerned about lough in part of Ireland

indicators.note: taking means the nobleman picks up the next item and carries it along after him
about means one word goes around the outside of the next

blocks.note: a count is a European nobleman
Y is the abbreviation for year
to care is to be concerned
L abbreviates lake, and lough is the Irish word for a lake

explanation.surface: A nobleman spends a year worrying over a lake somewhere in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Lough is the Irish word for a lake, so it takes the usual lake abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Clare is one of the counties of the Republic of Ireland, on its west coast, so it is a region of that island.

clue.text: In ruins, discern evidence of blaze

indicators.note: something in ruins is broken apart, so its letters are scattered and rebuilt

blocks.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Picking through ruined buildings, an investigator spots signs that there was a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashes and charred remains left behind show that something has burned, so they prove a fire happened.

clue.text: An associate member of Nato, perhaps

blocks.note: the indefinite article in its short form
a crony is a close companion or associate
M is a standard abbreviation for member

explanation.surface: A country that has an associate-member link to the North Atlantic alliance.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a diplomatic phrase, but the three words are separate pieces, and 'Nato, perhaps' is the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: NATO is formed from the initial letters of North Atlantic Treaty Organization, so it is one example of such a word.

clue.text: Lost, wandering around Norman city

indicators.note: wandering around suggests aimless movement, so the letters move into a new order

blocks.note: the four letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone lost, wandering about a city in Normandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint-Lô is a town in Normandy, northern France, heavily fought over in 1944.

clue.text: Potato and mouse (once tail removed) cooked as comfort food

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter, and once that is removed the word is cut short
cooked means mixed and processed, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, before its last letter goes

explanation.surface: An unappetising recipe in which a potato and a tailless mouse are cooked up.
explanation.walkthrough: MOUSE loses its E to give MOUS, and POTATO plus MOUS is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A warm bowl of this red soup is a classic soothing dish people turn to when unwell or low.

clue.text: Highest degree, English, old examination accepted, above board

indicators.note: something accepted is taken in, so the exam holds the other pieces inside it

blocks.note: to the nth degree means to the utmost
E is the abbreviation for English
the O level was a British school exam taken at about sixteen, replaced by the GCSE in 1988

explanation.surface: A report card listing a top degree, English and an old exam, all honestly earned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highest degree' suggests a university qualification, but it is the mathematical idiom 'to the nth degree'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases describe something honest and legitimate, done openly without trickery.

clue.text: Article ensuring independence abandoned when changing side

indicators.note: abandoned means the named letter is dropped and left behind
changing means the remaining letters alter their order

blocks.note: the definite article
taken as written
I is the abbreviation for independent or independence

explanation.surface: A political article about giving up independence after a change of allegiance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing side' reads as switching allegiance, but side is the definition: a sports team.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gunners is the nickname of Arsenal, a London football club, and a football team is called a side.

clue.text: Suggestive banter, perhaps, revealed in regressive corporations

indicators.note: regressive means going backwards, so the word is read from end to start

blocks.note: a corporation is old British slang for a large paunch, and tums are bellies

explanation.surface: Dirty jokes uncovered in backward-looking companies.
explanation.walkthrough: Corporations looks like businesses, but here it means big bellies.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewd or indecent talk is called this, and suggestive banter is one example of such material.

clue.text: French girl in beret attends dance

indicators.note: to dance is to move around, so the letters move into a new order

blocks.note: the twelve letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A French girl in a beret goes along to a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Bernadette Soubirous was a peasant girl from Lourdes whose visions made her a canonised saint.

clue.text: Diners’ sweet concoction?

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture, so these letters are blended into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the eleven letters to be rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the anagram gives the answer, and the full phrase describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Restaurant guests are served a sweet alcoholic drink with pudding, a blended product of the vintner.

clue.text: Prepare for Auld Lang Syne, with number going wonderfully

indicators.note: going means departing, so the named letter leaves the phrase

blocks.note: people singing this New Year song cross and join arms with their neighbours
N is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: Getting ready for the New Year singalong goes off wonderfully.
explanation.walkthrough: Auld Lang Syne is the Scottish song sung at New Year with arms linked in a circle; take N out of LINK EACH ARM.
explanation.definitionFit: Something working this way succeeds perfectly, as if by magic, so the idiom means superbly.

clue.text: How fell fat sort!?

blocks.note: surface reading: a question about how a plump person tumbled
setter's reading: the plump egg of the nursery rhyme, Humpty Dumpty, who sat on a wall and had a great fall; the phrase also means eccentric, hence the !?

explanation.walkthrough: The answer says where Humpty Dumpty fell from, and the '!?' hints at its other meaning, bizarre.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally describes a tumble from a garden barrier and idiomatically means bizarre or unconventional.

clue.text: ‘Poop a swear word?’ ‘Almost’ ‘That’s clear’

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: the poop is slang for the inside information
a cuss is a curse or swear word

explanation.surface: A bit of dialogue: someone asks whether poop counts as a swear word, gets 'almost', and is satisfied.
explanation.walkthrough: Poop looks like a mild rude word, but here it means information.
explanation.definitionFit: An image that is sharp rather than blurred is clear, as when a camera lens is properly adjusted.

clue.text: Think about taste? Oddly, it needs to be experienced

indicators.note: about means one word goes around the other, enclosing it
oddly means taking only the letters in odd-numbered places

blocks.note: to muse is to think or ponder
first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A food critic ponders flavour, then insists you have to try it yourself.
explanation.walkthrough: The kept letters slip in near the end of the thinking word, just before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something billed this way is so good that nobody should miss it, a show or sight everyone ought to catch.

clue.text: Embroils parents in strife

indicators.note: strife is conflict and disorder, so the letters are thrown out of order

blocks.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone drags mother and father into a family quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: To embroil someone is to catch them up in a difficult situation, much as a snare traps prey.

clue.text: Gags and locks away

blocks.note: first meaning: silences someone
second meaning: confines or closes up securely

explanation.walkthrough: Gags might be jokes, but here it is a verb: silences.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both silencing a person and closing a building or prisoner securely in.

clue.text: Cool to reach number one, perhaps, for musician

indicators.note: to reach means the first piece extends onward to join the next

blocks.note: to ice something is to cool it
one is a cube number, since one times one times one is one; perhaps marks it as an example

explanation.surface: A cool artist on the way to topping the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: Number one looks like a chart-topper, but it is the number 1, an example of a cube.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice Cube is the stage name of an American rapper, a founder of the hip-hop group N.W.A.

clue.text: Cold, topless, in Spain and Portugal

definitions.note: a phrase standing for an adjective

indicators.note: topless means without its top, which in a down entry is the first letter

blocks.note: Siberian describes bitter cold, as in Siberian weather

explanation.surface: Someone sunbathing topless in Iberia finds it chilly.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iberian Peninsula is the landmass shared by the two countries, so the adjective describes things found there.

clue.text: What’s blazing in zest, purée, etc?

definitions.text: What’s blazing in zest, purée, etc?

indicators.note: something blazing is wildly agitated by fire, so the letters are thrown about

blocks.note: the twelve letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook asks which item is on fire among the zest, the purée and the other ingredients.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the dish: thin pancakes in an orange-zest sauce, flamed with liqueur at the table.
explanation.definitionFit: This French dessert of pancakes in orange butter sauce is famously set alight with liqueur before serving.

clue.text: Estonian regularly visited Italian hot spot

indicators.note: regularly means at fixed intervals, taking every other letter

blocks.note: first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A traveller from Estonia keeps going back to a favourite Italian resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Etna is an active Sicilian volcano, literally a place in Italy that is very hot.

clue.text: Art gallery's thank-you note

blocks.note: ta is informal British for thank you
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A gallery sends a note of thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tate is a group of national galleries of art in Britain, including Tate Modern in London.

clue.text: Early on, a harpooner and boy?

definitions.text: Early on, a harpooner and boy?

indicators.note: early on points to the start of each word, so its opening letter is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A riddle about a whaling ship's crew: early in life, someone was a harpooner and a mere lad.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes Captain Ahab of Moby-Dick, who was a whale hunter and boy in his early years at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The obsessive captain of Melville's novel hunted the white whale with a harpoon, and went to sea young.

clue.text: Evergreen Shakespearean killer, not half: 'Ides isn't tragic'

indicators.note: not half means only half of each word is kept and the rest discarded

blocks.note: Cleopatra kills herself with a poisonous snake in Antony and Cleopatra
taken as written
taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean villain insists the Ides of March is not a tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ides of March evokes Caesar's killers, but the killer is Cleopatra's snake; then the first half of each quoted word follows.
explanation.definitionFit: This hardy leafy houseplant keeps its foliage all year round, so it is an evergreen.

clue.text: African national? Not so: African nation

indicators.note: not means the following letters are excluded from the word

blocks.note: a Somali is a person from Somalia
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person is from Africa, is told no, and then names a country there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not so' reads as a denial, but SO is the letters removed from SOMALI.
explanation.definitionFit: Mali is a landlocked country in West Africa, whose capital is Bamako.

clue.text: Old writers mentioned before, adopting eastern magic words

indicators.note: adopting means taking something in, so the letters hold another inside them

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
pens are writing instruments
E is the abbreviation for eastern
the same refers back to something already mentioned

explanation.surface: Old authors cited earlier took up Eastern spells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mentioned before' works like 'the same' in legal writing, meaning the thing just referred to.
explanation.definitionFit: Ali Baba speaks this phrase to open the robbers' cave in the Arabian Nights, a spell to unlock a door.
